name: net.connection.activate
doc: Connect a profile {uuid, device?} (NetworkManager ActivateConnection; the device is an interface name, else NetworkManager picks one); event net.changed.

name: net.connection.add
doc: Add a profile {settings} ({group: {key: value}}, typed as NetworkManager's D-Bus settings; a uuid is made when it has none) with AddConnection2, saved to disk; answers {uuid, path}.

name: net.connection.deactivate
doc: Disconnect the active connection of a profile {uuid} (DeactivateConnection).

name: net.connection.delete
doc: Forget a profile {uuid} (Settings.Connection Delete).

name: net.connection.get
doc: Every setting of a profile {uuid} as JSON (byte arrays such as the SSID as numbers, address-data, route-data; keys WinPoint does not edit included), plus {summary, unsaved, filename}.

name: net.connection.update
doc: Change a profile {uuid, settings, reapply?}: the changed keys ({group: {key: value or null}}, a null group removes it) merged into NetworkManager's own settings, every other key kept, saved with Update2 (to disk); a change of a secret carries the stored secrets along; reapply (default true) applies it to the active connection (Device.Reapply, else a reconnect).

name: net.connections
doc: The profiles {type?} (an NM type such as 802-11-wireless, or wifi / ethernet): uuid, id, type, autoconnect, timestamp, metered, permissions, the SSID and key management of Wi-Fi, whether and where it is active; the active ones first, then the last used.

name: net.connectivity.set
doc: Turn NetworkManager's connectivity checking on or off {on} (ConnectivityCheckEnabled, polkit network-control).

name: net.device.setEnabled
doc: Turn a network adapter {iface, on} off (Device.Disconnect) or on (ActivateConnection of the best profile), as GNOME's wired switch.

name: net.devices
doc: The network adapters {accessPoints?, scan?}: type, state, driver, vendor and model, MAC addresses, speed or bit rate, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, gateway and DNS, the active connection, the profiles it can use, for Wi-Fi the access point (band, channel, security) and with accessPoints every one in range; plus NetworkManager's Wi-Fi, mobile broadband and connectivity-check switches.

name: net.hotspot.get
doc: The mobile hotspot {secrets?}: available (a Wi-Fi adapter), iface, apCapable, bands, active, state, configured (a stored hotspot profile: Wi-Fi in mode ap or adhoc with IPv4 shared, as GNOME's), uuid, ssid, band (a, bg or empty), keyMgmt, security; password and the WIFI: QR text only with secrets (GetSecrets, which may ask for the password); without a stored hotspot the computer's name and a new random key; uplink {id, type, iface} (the primary connection) and sameAdapter.

name: net.hotspot.start
doc: Turn the mobile hotspot on {ssid?, password?, band?, iface?, activate?}: the stored hotspot profile changed (Update2 merge; null keeps a value) or GNOME's new one made ("Hotspot", mode ap, IPv4 shared, IPv6 ignored, no autoconnect, WPA2/WPA/WEP by the adapter, the computer's name and a random key by default), then activated (activate false only saves it: Windows' Edit while the hotspot is off). band is a (5 GHz), bg (2.4 GHz) or empty (any); event net.changed hotspot.

name: net.hotspot.stop
doc: Turn the mobile hotspot off {} (DeactivateConnection of every active hotspot; nothing when none runs).

name: net.modem.apns
doc: The access points of a mobile operator {mcc, mnc} from mobile-broadband-provider-info's serviceproviders.xml: providers [{name, country, apns: [{apn, name, usage, username, password, auth, dns}]}].

name: net.modem.changePin
doc: Change the SIM PIN {modem, old, new} (Sim.ChangePin); interactive.

name: net.modem.get
doc: The modems of ModemManager {}: manufacturer, model, firmware, IMEI, numbers, state, failedReason, unlockRequired and unlockRetries, technologies, networkType (5G/4G/3G/2G), signal, supported and current modes, SIM (iccid, imsi, operator, mcc, mnc), SIM slots and the primary one, registration, operator, pinEnabled, NetworkManager's iface and state, and the gsm profiles for its SIM (uuid, id, apn, autoconnect, homeOnly, attach, auth, active); plus wwanEnabled. available false without ModemManager.

name: net.modem.register
doc: Choose the mobile network {modem, operator?} (Modem3gpp.Register; no operator or an empty one: automatic); interactive.

name: net.modem.scan
doc: Scan for mobile networks {modem} (Modem3gpp.Scan, which can take a minute; interactive): networks [{code, name, short, status, networkType}], the current one first.

name: net.modem.setModes
doc: Set the network mode {modem, allowed, preferred} (MMModemMode bits, one of the modem's SupportedModes; Modem.SetCurrentModes); interactive.

name: net.modem.setPin
doc: Turn the SIM PIN lock on or off {modem, enabled, pin} (Sim.EnablePin); interactive.

name: net.modem.setPrimarySlot
doc: Use another SIM slot {modem, slot} (1-based; Modem.SetPrimarySimSlot, the modem restarts); interactive.

name: net.modem.unlock
doc: Unlock a modem's SIM {modem, pin} (Sim.SendPin) or {modem, puk, newPin} (Sim.SendPuk); modem is its ModemManager path; interactive.

name: net.radios.set
doc: Turn Wi-Fi and/or mobile broadband on or off {wifi?, wwan?} (NetworkManager WirelessEnabled, WwanEnabled).

name: net.vpn.import
doc: Import a VPN file {path, type?} (type openvpn, wireguard or vpnc, else from the file: a WireGuard [Interface], an OpenVPN configuration or .ovpn, a Cisco .pcf) with libnm offline parsing then interactive AddConnection2, as GNOME's Import from file; a WireGuard file is named after its interface (wg0.conf); answers {uuid, type}.

name: net.vpn.plugins
doc: The installed NetworkManager VPN plugins {} from /usr/lib/NetworkManager/VPN and /etc/NetworkManager/VPN *.name: name, service (vpn.service-type), program, editor, import (its libnm plugin can import files); and wireguard (NetworkManager's own type).

name: net.wifi.hidden
doc: Connect to a hidden network {ssid, security, secrets?, autoconnect?, iface?, hidden?}: security open, owe, wep, wep-passphrase, leap, dynamic-wep, wpa-psk, sae or wpa-eap, secrets the 802-11-wireless-security and 802-1x keys; AddAndActivateConnection2 with 802-11-wireless.hidden (hidden false: a network in the list that needs the WEP or 802.1X fields, as GNOME's Wi-Fi dialog for an access point).

name: net.wifi.secrets
doc: A Wi-Fi profile's security key {uuid} (GetSecrets, which may ask for the password): {ssid, keyMgmt, key, hidden, qr}, qr the WIFI: text of GNOME's Share Network QR code (null for an enterprise network).

name: sharing.media.folders.set
doc: Set the shared folders {folders} (full paths) in ~/.config/rygel.conf as GNOME writes it (the system's /etc/rygel.conf as the start, comments kept, upnp-enabled true, Tracker off, MediaExport on, the user's Music, Videos and Pictures as @MUSIC@, @VIDEOS@, @PICTURES@); event sharing.changed media.

name: sharing.media.get
doc: Media streaming (GNOME's Media Sharing, rygel) {}: available (rygel installed), running (gsd Sharing answers), status (available, offline, disabled-mobile-broadband, disabled-low-security), currentNetwork, currentNetworkName, carrierType, enabled (shared on the current network), networks [{uuid, name, carrier}] (ListNetworks rygel), folders (rygel.conf MediaExport uris, the special folders expanded).

name: sharing.media.networks.remove
doc: Stop media streaming on one network {uuid} (gsd Sharing DisableService rygel <uuid>); event sharing.changed media.

name: sharing.media.set
doc: Turn media streaming on or off for the current network {on} (gsd Sharing EnableService rygel / DisableService rygel <current network>); event sharing.changed media.

name: sharing.rdp.credentials.get
doc: The RDP sign-in details {system?}: {username, password} (null when none are stored) of the user daemon (grdctl status --show-credentials, the login keyring; it may ask to unlock it) or, with system true, of the system daemon for remote login (org.gnome.RemoteDesktop.Configuration GetCredentials, interactive: polkit configure-system-daemon).

name: sharing.rdp.credentials.set
doc: Store the user daemon's RDP sign-in details {username, password} (grdctl rdp set-credentials <username>, the password on its standard input; no control characters, the user name not starting with -); event sharing.changed rdp.

name: sharing.rdp.fingerprint
doc: The encryption fingerprint of Desktop Sharing's certificate {}: {fingerprint} (SHA-256 of the DER of tls-cert as AB:CD:..., null without a certificate), as GNOME's Verify Fingerprint dialog.

name: sharing.rdp.get
doc: Desktop Sharing (gnome-remote-desktop's user daemon) {}: available (its schema), enabled and viewOnly (org.gnome.desktop.remote-desktop.rdp enable, view-only), port (the running daemon's own, also a negotiated one, else the key), configuredPort, negotiatePort, running, unit (gnome-remote-desktop.service of the user manager: exists, fileState, active), hostname, certificate and fingerprint (SHA-256 of tls-cert, AB:CD:...), grdctl and tls (whether grdctl and libgnutls.so.30 are there).

name: sharing.rdp.set
doc: Turn Desktop Sharing on or off {on}, as GNOME Settings: on = the TLS certificate made with GnuTLS when tls-cert/tls-key do not load (~/.local/share/gnome-remote-desktop/certificates/rdp-tls.crt and .key, C=US,CN=GNOME), enable true, the user name and a new password stored through grdctl when the keyring has none, then the user unit gnome-remote-desktop.service started and enabled (systemd user manager StartUnit + EnableUnitFiles); off = enable false, the unit stopped and disabled. Answers {on, credentials: kept|stored|failed}; event sharing.changed rdp.

name: sharing.rdp.system.credentials.set
doc: Set Remote Login's sign-in details {username, password} (SetCredentials, interactive); event sharing.changed system.

name: sharing.rdp.system.get
doc: Remote Login (gnome-remote-desktop's system daemon, org.gnome.RemoteDesktop.Configuration on the system bus, D-Bus activated) {}: available, enabled, port, certificate, fingerprint (the daemon's TlsFingerprint as AB:CD:...), hostname.

name: sharing.rdp.system.set
doc: Turn Remote Login on or off {on}: on = when the daemon has no certificate, GNOME's new pair imported (ImportCertificate with both files as descriptors), then Enable(); off = Disable(); interactive (polkit configure-system-daemon; the daemon runs gnome-remote-desktop-enable-service itself). Answers {on, imported}; event sharing.changed system.

name: sharing.ssh.get
doc: Secure Shell {}: installed (openssh-server: /usr/sbin/sshd or its units), on (ssh.socket or ssh.service running), enabled, socket and service (exists, fileState, active), installing, command (ssh <user>@<host>, GNOME's SSH Login Command).

name: sharing.ssh.install
doc: Install openssh-server {} (Windows' Add an optional feature) through PackageKit: Resolve (not installed, this architecture), then InstallPackages (only trusted), hints interactive=true and the UI locale; polkit package-install asks for the password. Waits until it finishes, with events sharing.changed {what: sshInstall, percentage}; answers {installed, package}.

name: sharing.ssh.set
doc: Turn the OpenSSH server on or off {on} through systemd's system manager, interactive (polkit manage-units / manage-unit-files): on = StartUnit + EnableUnitFiles of ssh.socket when systemd has it, else ssh.service (amendment 35); off = StopUnit + DisableUnitFiles of both. Event sharing.changed ssh.
